gap: No result ChatGPT got prices the flash and the diffuser together. A Godox TT685 II ($129), the S-R1 round-head adapter ($9) and the AK-R1 magnetic kit, which includes a diffusion ball ($59), cost $197 at MoLight on 2026-11-08. The V1 ($258.99) plus the AK-R11 dome ($11.90) costs $270.89 at Pro Photo Supply. The newer V1 Pro ($329) and V100 ($349) cost $70–$90 more than the V1 before any dome.
standout_why: I compared against the cited B&H AK-R11 page and the top result cameraegg.org 'Best Diffuser for Godox V1 Flash' (2026-10-09). B&H's AK-R11 page returned 403 to me, so I can't say what it states. Cameraegg prices only the diffusers (AK-R11 $7.90 B&H, AK-R22 $26.90, ML-CD15 $29, AK-R1 $49/$59) and assumes you already own a V1. It gives no flash price, no guide numbers and no stops of light loss. It also never mentions that a rectangular-head speedlight can take the magnetic dome through the $9 S-R1 adapter. None of the 16 results gives a flash-plus-dome total.
decides: The V1 + AK-R11 pick ChatGPT gave holds for someone who wants a round head that takes the dome directly. For a budget shopper it does not hold: the TT685 II + S-R1 + AK-R1 route is $73.89 cheaper and includes a grid, snoot and barn doors. The V1 Pro and V100 only make sense if the sub-flash (V1 Pro) or the 100 Ws output (V100) is worth $70–$90 more.

B&H prices for the AK-R11, V1 and the 'Diffusers for Godox V1' page: B&H returned 403 to both WebFetch attempts, and the curl attempt needed approval and was not run.

Godox's own compatibility statement that the separate AK-R11 (not the AK-R1 kit's diffusion ball) fits the S-R1: only retailer search snippets (Vistek, Videoguys) claim it, and Vistek and PetaPixel returned 403. A cheaper TT685 II + S-R1 + AK-R11 total of $149.90 is therefore left out.
Guide numbers for the V1 and V1 Pro from Godox's page or manual: no godox.com page surfaced, and retailer figures conflict (28 m vs 76 m).
